clue.text: Sex for Roman philosopher is noble

parts.note: sex is the Latin word for six, which in Roman numerals is VI
Auguste Comte, French founder of positivism

explanation.surface: A sexual scandal involving an ancient Roman thinker is pinned on an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' looks like the English word, but it is Latin for six; 'for Roman' tells you to translate and write it as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicomte is the French rank equivalent to a viscount, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Hip liberal philosopher — his work is decorative

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in
A. J. Ayer, British logical positivist

explanation.surface: A trendy, broad-minded thinker turns out to produce ornamental work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets decorative pieces into a surface, as in marquetry, does ornamental work.

clue.text: Head of Oundle has great final term

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so take the first of Oundle

parts.note: mega is slang for great

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Oundle, an English public school, enjoys a superb last term before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Oundle is an English boarding school, so 'Head' first reads as its headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end of a series, the last item.

clue.text: Slept so badly in a state of deshabille

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of the two words are put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who slept poorly is found half-dressed in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Deshabille means being partly or carelessly dressed, and bare-chested fits that state.

clue.text: Philosopher, one working a large amount

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, English utilitarian
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: A thinker who has a job earns a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand is used loosely for any huge quantity.

clue.text: Plain dancing? We're told why a ball may be so

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word plain is rearranged
we're told means heard spoken, so the word why stands for its sound

parts.note: the word why is spoken just like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks, of plain dancing, why a ball would be involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges PLAIN into INPLA; 'We're told' turns 'why' into the letter it sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball still live in a game, not out of bounds, is described this way.

clue.text: Doctor or sleepy nurses run kind of hospital

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so one piece goes inside the other
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of or sleepy are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A doctor or a drowsy nurse runs some sort of hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'nurses' look like hospital staff but are the anagram and insertion signals; R goes inside the rearranged OR SLEEPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper colony or hospital for people with leprosy is a specific type of medical institution.

clue.text: A canoe travelling around one large group of islands

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the next piece
travelling letters move around, so a canoe is rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A canoe paddles round a single island in a big archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges A CANOE into OCEANA, which goes 'around' I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the region of the Pacific taking in Australasia, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia.

clue.text: Acclaim actor lacking refinement in London park

parts.note: to clap is to applaud, acclaim
a ham is an overacting performer
common means vulgar, lacking refinement

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated actor is cheered in a London park.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham Common is a large open green space in south London.

clue.text: This is a reminder to invest pounds

indicators.note: to invest means to cover or clothe, so the reminder wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A note prompting someone to put money into an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the clue itself, which is what the answer is; 'invest' looks financial but means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: The words you are reading form the hint the solver works from, so 'This' points at itself.

clue.text: Sanctimonious lines by philosopher, a junkie

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
Karl Popper, philosopher of science

explanation.surface: A preachy thinker beside a few lines of text turns out to be an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' hints at cocaine, but here it is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually takes tablets or drugs is an addict, a junkie.

clue.text: Dance suggestively, in extremely giddy tempo

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters of giddy

parts.note: rate means speed, tempo

explanation.surface: Someone dances provocatively at a very dizzy pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve the hips in a sensual way is to move erotically on the dance floor.

clue.text: Philosopher concerned with small units

parts.note: Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher
on means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: A thinker preoccupied with little things.
explanation.definitionFit: Platoons are subdivisions of a company in an army, military units.

clue.text: Clothing collection and tea picked up by philosopher

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word tea stands for its sound

parts.note: the word tea is spoken just like the letter T
Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Genevan philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher collects a bundle of clothes and a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like collecting, but it is the signal for a sound-alike: 'tea' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's outfit and linen gathered for her marriage form a set of garments.

clue.text: British philosopher welcomed by German and not hindered

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so the German word wraps round the rest

parts.note: und is German for and
John Locke, English empiricist

explanation.surface: A British thinker received by a German goes unhindered.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear of obstruction means free to pass, unobstructed.

clue.text: King swallows drop of Lemsip, catching a chill

indicators.note: swallows means takes in, so the king surrounds the next piece

parts.note: rex is Latin for king

indicators.note: catching means picking up alongside, so a joins the drop of Lemsip inside the king
a drop is a small amount, the first letter of Lemsip

explanation.surface: A king takes a dose of Lemsip, a British cold remedy, having caught a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemsip is a British hot lemon cold-and-flu drink. 'chill' looks like an ailment but is the verb, as in chill out.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill, in the slang sense, is to unwind and take it easy.

clue.text: Actress in Ultimo bra, gracefully twirling

indicators.note: twirling says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actress is wearing an Ultimo bra, a lingerie brand, as she spins elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run sits inside 'Ultimo bra, gracefully' and 'twirling' turns it round. Ultimo is a British lingerie brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Salt in wonderful starter of tabbouleh getting consumed

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent, wonderful

indicators.note: starter means the opening letter of tabbouleh

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Salt goes into a wonderful tabbouleh starter that gets eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an acetate is a salt or ester of acetic acid.

clue.text: A friend meets Mike using letters of introduction?

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
mic is short for microphone, informally a mike

explanation.surface: A pal is introduced to a man called Mike by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters of introduction' usually means references; here it means the initial letters of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from initial letters, like NATO, is built from the letters that open other words.

clue.text: Look at cracking cryptic done like a Cyclops?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the next piece goes inside
cryptic means puzzling or scrambled, so the letters of done are rearranged

parts.note: to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Look at how a cryptic crossword is cracked, finished by a one-eyed giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' is the anagram signal here, not a description of the puzzle; 'Look at' is the verb to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops of Greek myth had a single eye in the middle of his forehead.

clue.text: One first rings a doctor, a specialist in feet

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: first written as a numeral is 1st, which reads as the letters IST
MB is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A patient phones a doctor first, the one who specialises in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' as 1st gives IST, which 'rings' A, MB and I (one). 'feet' looks like a chiropodist's concern, but means metrical feet in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet who writes in iambs, the metrical foot of short then long syllables, works in feet.

clue.text: Occasion to eat a piece of cake

definitions.meaning: an outdoor meal is an occasion for eating

explanation.surface: An occasion to eat a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an outdoor meal and, informally, a very easy task.

clue.text: Supply me with dosh in search for pleasure

indicators.note: supply read as supple-ly suggests bending, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be given money in their pursuit of pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but read as 'supplely' it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophy and lifestyle of pursuing enjoyment above all is a quest for gratification.

clue.text: Unearth erstwhile philosopher

parts.note: ex means former, erstwhile
David Hume, Scottish empiricist

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a philosopher who is long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig a body out of the ground is to disinter it.

clue.text: Man turned on philosopher

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, a man

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the cricket word is read backwards

parts.note: the on side in cricket is also called leg

explanation.surface: A man turns against a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Hegel was the German idealist thinker behind dialectics.

clue.text: Roman philosopher running into virgin

indicators.note: into says the philosopher and running go inside the virgin

parts.note: Mary, the Virgin Mary
Immanuel Kant, German philosopher
on means running, operating

explanation.surface: A Roman thinker bumps into a virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony was the Roman general and ally of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Expression of pleasure as tedium's cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a grind is tedious, laborious work

explanation.surface: A smile appears when boredom is brought to an early end.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile shows on the face when someone is happy.

clue.text: Finding court composer's given precedence

indicators.note: given precedence means put in front, so the composer comes before the court

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A court discovers an opera composer has been put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's decision in a case is its finding.

clue.text: Flatter hulk stripping off during a tryst

indicators.note: during means within, so the stripped piece sits inside

parts.note: a date is a romantic meeting, a tryst

indicators.note: stripping off the outside leaves the middle of hulk

explanation.surface: A big man undresses during a romantic encounter, piling on compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping off' removes the outer letters of HULK to give UL.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone excessively is to fawn on them, to lavish compliments.
